practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Effective July 15, 2026 (2026 Ky. Acts ch. 94, SB 116): a PA may not provide any service until a supervision agreement on the board's standardized form is completed, signed by the supervising physician and PA, and in effect. A copy and every amendment must be furnished to and kept on file by the board and kept at the primary practice location. The supervising physician must be board approved; a physician may supervise no more than four PAs at a time. Licensed facilities may designate alternate supervising physicians. No fixed renewal interval for the agreement is set in the statute; the board is to set renewal procedures by regulation. KBML FAQ: since July 15, 2026 the board files but no longer approves agreements; an amended agreement is resubmitted (no fee); if the supervising physician stops supervising, the PA notifies the board in writing within three business days and may not practice until a new application and agreement are in.
practice.notes: PAs may not practice independently (KRS 311.858(8) as amended 2026). KRS 311.860 (separate practice location rules) was repealed by the 2026 Act.

prescribing.stateCsRegistrationRequired: KASPER (Kentucky PDMP) registration required before controlled substance prescribing; the statute also says 'any other applicable state controlled substance regulatory authority' without naming one
prescribing.ceForPrescribers: Separate board approval of prescriptive authority for controlled substances: at least 1 year of PA practice, application signed by the supervising physician, board approval notice, DEA registration and KASPER registration. Schedule II to V allowed with supply limits (narcotic Schedule II 72 hours; hydrocodone combinations, nonnarcotic Schedule II and Schedule III 30 days; Schedule IV and V six months; benzodiazepines and carisoprodol 30 days). 7.5 hours CS CE per cycle.

rn.renewalDeadline: October 31 each year (licensure period November 1 to October 31)
rn.ceNotes: Each earning period (November 1 to October 31) the nurse validates competency by one method: 14 contact hours; or current national certification or recertification; or a research project, peer-reviewed publication or 120-hour preceptorship; or 7 contact hours plus a satisfactory employment evaluation. Section 5 mandates apply under every method.

aprn.title: APRN (Advanced Practice Registered Nurse), designated certified nurse practitioner with a population focus
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: separate APRN license that expires or lapses with the RN license or multistate privilege
aprn.renewalNotes: Annual, same October 31 expiration as the RN license; renew the RN license or privilege on active status first
aprn.ceNotes: No separate APRN hour total; the RN validation method applies (14 contact hours, or national certification or another listed method plus the Section 5 mandates). Every APRN needs 5 pharmacology contact hours each year (KRS 314.073(9)).

topicMandates.topic: Pharmacology (at least 3 of the 5 hours on pain management or addiction disorders)

topicMandates.appliesTo: APRNs with a DEA registration, before the next scheduled DEA registration after June 27, 2023 (recent graduates and prior DATA waiver training may satisfy it)

prescribing.separateAuthorityRegistration: CAPA-NS and CAPA-CS collaborative agreements are notified to the board (no separate prescribing licence); CAPA-CS exemption requires a board good-standing review and written notice
prescribing.pharmacologyCeForPrescribers: 5 contact hours pharmacology every year for every APRN; at least 3 on pain management or addiction disorders if DEA registered with a PDMP account
prescribing.controlledSubstanceCe: 3 of the 5 annual pharmacology hours on pain management or addiction disorders (DEA registrants); one-time 8 hours substance use disorder training for DEA registrants
prescribing.stateCsRegistrationRequired: KASPER master account registration within 30 days of DEA registration and before prescribing controlled substances; no separate state CS registration named in KRS 314.042

practice.transitionToPracticeHours: 4 years of prescribing (not hours): CAPA-NS for nonscheduled legend drugs until 4 years of prescribing in the population focus; CAPA-CS for Schedule II to V until 4 years of controlled substance prescribing plus a board review
practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: CAPA-NS: written, signed by APRN and a Kentucky physician in the same or similar specialty; APRN notifies KBN of its existence and the physician's name; copy at each practice site; after 4 years the APRN notifies KBN and may stop. CAPA-CS: on the standardized CAPA-CS form; KBN notified and forwards to KBML; copy at each site; first year quarterly meetings and next three years twice-yearly meetings to review the reverse KASPER report, records kept one year past expiration; rescission on 30 days written notice with KBN notified. After 4 years with DEA and KASPER maintained, the APRN requests a KBN good-standing review and may not prescribe controlled substances without a CAPA-CS until KBN notifies in writing.

unverified: The KY PA renewal dates (February 1 to March 31 of the renewal year, grace to April 30) come from the KBML PA FAQ PDF, a board document. The regulation that sets the PA renewal date was not loaded.

201 KAR 9:360 (effective June 16, 2026) does not yet list the pediatric ingestion or inhalation hour that KRS 311.844(3)(b)3 adds from July 15, 2026. The statute applies it to all PAs; the KBML FAQ applies it to prescribers within the 7.5 hours.
201 KAR 9:360 Section 2(3) still requires 12 addiction medicine hours for buprenorphine prescribers. No source loaded shows whether KBML still enforces it after the federal X waiver ended.
The PA supervision agreement has no fixed renewal interval in KRS 311.854 as amended. The implementing regulation was not loaded.

KRS 311.858 and 314.042 name no separate Kentucky state controlled substance registration for PAs or APRNs, only KASPER. KRS 311.858(4)(b)4 also says 'any other applicable state controlled substance regulatory authority' without naming one.

201 KAR 20:215 (effective July 30, 2025) does not yet include the KRS 314.073(6)(b) pediatric ingestion or inhalation hour (statute effective July 15, 2026). Start date and documentation rules for it are not yet in regulation.

The suicide prevention mandate (201 KAR 20:215 Section 5(5)(d)) gives no completion deadline for nurses licensed before July 15, 2024 who have not done it. Section 5(7) sets October 31, 2027 only for the dementia hour.
The 'reduced' practice authority label is inferred from the CAPA-NS and CAPA-CS requirements in KRS 314.042; the board does not use that label.
verificationNotes: All KY facts re-loaded 2026-10-01 from apps.legislature.ky.gov (KRS 311.844 effective July 15, 2026; KRS 314.042 effective April 10, 2026; KRS 314.073 effective July 15, 2026; 201 KAR 9:360 effective June 16, 2026; 201 KAR 20:215 effective July 30, 2025), 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 94 and the KBML PA FAQ.
corrections: KY PA pediatric ingestion hour: the statute lists it as item 3 under (3)(b), at the same level as the prescriber item 2, so it applies to every PA. The KBML FAQ (2026) folds it into the 7.5 prescriber hours. appliesTo now records both readings.
KY PA dementia hour: added the KBML FAQ timing for existing licensees (before the end of the first renewal cycle after July 1, 2025).
KY PA buprenorphine 12 hours: 201 KAR 9:360 was amended effective June 16, 2026 and still contains Section 2(3), so the rule is current and in force. Removed from unverified.
KY PA agreement: added KBML FAQ facts. Since July 15, 2026 the board files agreements without approving them, amendments are resubmitted, and a supervisor change is reported within 3 business days.

KY RN suicide prevention: WRONG. The October 31, 2027 deadline in 201 KAR 20:215 Section 5(7) is for subsection (5)(c), Alzheimer's and dementia, not suicide prevention. Moved the deadline to the dementia mandate. Suicide prevention now reads: one time; new licensees within 3 years; no stated deadline for other existing licensees.
KY NLC fact: replaced the indirect evidence (a 201 KAR 20:056 renewal form name) with the compact statute itself, KRS 314.475, effective July 20, 2017. KRS 314.470 (old compact) was repealed in 2017.
